exit_criterion: Two claims, each demonstrated over HTTP by tests/exit_run_phase5.py and recorded in docs/phase-5/exit-run.md. (1) On the Quadram Institute fresh-meat FTIR set (three classes, CC0), outliers are flagged and excluded with the exclusion recorded in lineage, variables are selected, and PLS-DA, SIMCA, LDA and kNN are compared under the same stratified cross-validation, each matching its reference within stated tolerance; separately, PCR and variable-selected PLS on Tecator match their references. (2) A file of each new format (MAT, SPC, SPA, ASD) from the open sources in docs/decisions/0006 imports through the application and matches its source's own export or reference.
decisions: 2026-10-02. Classifiers: PLS-DA becomes multi-class (on a PLS2 kernel), plus SIMCA, LDA and kNN. SVM is deferred: it needs a hand-written QP solver.
2026-10-02. Outlier detection flags; the user excludes. An exclusion is a derived DatasetVersion (excluded_samples, derived_from), never a pipeline step that drops rows.
2026-10-02. Variable selection: VIP or coefficient threshold, iPLS and CARS, each applied as an explicit select_variables step. Genetic algorithms are deferred.
2026-10-02. File formats: MATLAB .mat, Thermo Galactic SPC, Thermo OMNIC SPA, ASD. Each with a real, licensed fixture.
2026-10-02. Smoothing: moving average, median, Gaussian, Whittaker.

2026-10-02. Unchanged: scikit-learn and chemotools stay development dependencies. Every kernel is hand-written; parity is against a reference library, mdatools, or recorded not_compared with a reason.
2026-10-02. One release, v1.1.0, at the end of the phase. Phase 4's timed exit run stays closed as recorded in docs/phase-4/.

2026-10-02. All Phase 5 development data comes from open, licensed datasets on the internet, downloaded into the gitignored dataset/ folder; CI-facing copies are committed as small fixtures with their licence. Sources and rules: docs/decisions/0006-phase-5-data-sources.md.

features.evidence: 2026-10-02. `uv run pytest`: `931 passed, 1 skipped`. tests/test_validation.py: a stratified K-fold partitions, keeps every level's count per fold within one and fold sizes within one, for K = 2, 3, 5; it follows from its seed; unshuffled it reproduces the section 8.7 worked example; stratified train/test holds out ceil(test_size * n_g) of each level; a one-member level and a test size that empties a level are refused by name. tests/test_executor.py: TrainTestSplit and KFoldSplit with stratify_by resolve to the kernel's folds on Tecator with an unbalanced three-level column, each level's held-out count within one of its share; a missing column and a too-small level are refused naming the node, the column and the level; an unstratified K-fold dumps exactly the JSON it did before (`exclude_if`), so no stored cache key moves, and the contract fixture test passes unchanged. Proof: with src/ reverted and the new tests kept, both modules fail at collection (the stratified kernels do not exist). The sklearn StratifiedKFold difference is stated in the parity report's fold-assignment row (not_compared), regenerated with `uv run python -m tests.parity_report` (120 claims). ruff, ruff format, mypy (70 files) clean. `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test`: 140 passed, including stratifiableColumns. `pnpm build` then `pnpm exec playwright test`: 74 passed (2.3m), including inspector.spec.ts 'a k-fold is stratified by a class column chosen from a dropdown': the select offers none and fat_class, the saved split carries stratify_by, the run completes the split node, and none puts it back.

features.evidence: 2026-10-02. Design decided in the work: an exclusion materialises a derived version (kept rows written as a new array, its own content hash, derived_from the parent, excluded_samples = parent row indices) rather than masking rows in place, so the executor, folds, payloads and sample ids need no change; recorded in design/data-model.md and the DatasetVersion field description. `uv run pytest`: `945 passed, 1 skipped`. tests/test_api.py: POST /datasets/{id}/versions writes version 2 with rows 1 and 6 gone from the array, ids and targets, deduplicated and sorted excluded_samples, a new content hash, and moves the pipeline source onto it; pointing the source back through PUT /pipelines/current restores the parent; an empty, out-of-range or too-large exclusion is refused 422 invalid_exclusion with the reason. tests/test_artifact.py: the manifest's dataset block carries derived_from and excluded_samples (null and [] when nothing was excluded). tests/test_report.py: a run on a derived version prints '2 rows of version <parent>: 4, 9'. Proof: with src/ reverted and the new tests kept, the derive, refusal, artifact and report tests fail (7 failed); the restore test drives an existing endpoint. ruff, mypy (71 files) clean. `pnpm test`: 142 passed, lineage.test.ts now naming a source's version_id change (the diff compared only step/spec and missed it; fixed in diff.ts). `pnpm build` then `pnpm exec playwright test`: 75 passed, walkthrough.spec.ts excluding A002 and A005 from the dataset table, seeing v2 28x24 with '2 excluded from v1' and 'Left out of v1: A002, A005', running PCA on 28 samples, and restoring v1.

features.title: A run started while a save is in flight runs what was saved

features.evidence: 2026-10-03. Root cause of #291 (Windows docs-examples, 1 of 5 complete after Done) and of #298's first ubuntu run (4 of 6): Run was clicked while the Save PUT was in flight, the server executed the recipe from before the save, the job reported Done, and the new nodes stayed not run. useSavePipeline now carries a shared mutation key; Shell disables Run while any save is pending and startRun waits for pending saves before posting. `pnpm test`: 144 passed. `pnpm build` then `pnpm exec playwright test`: 77 passed, including walkthrough.spec.ts 'a run started while a save is in flight runs what was saved', which delays the PUT by 1 s with page.route and clicks Save then Run. Proof: with frontend/src reverted and the test kept, it fails 'Expected: 7, Received: 6' - the CI signature.
features.notes: Found while fixing #296; depends on it only because the test adds a step from the side list to a chain ending in PCA.
